about.title: Diamond Bar Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Diamond Bar sits where the SR-60 and SR-57 corridors meet local streets like Diamond Bar Boulevard and Golden Springs Drive, and public records show hundreds of injury collisions here each year, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing up often. A crash on any of these roads can leave you dealing with medical appointments, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster all at once. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge fees; we simply connect injured Diamond Bar residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of the collision, from freeway on-ramp merges to intersection collisions on surface streets. The attorney you're matched with works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your case results in a recovery. Our role ends once that connection is made and the legal work is in capable, independent hands.

whyChoose.title: Why Acting Early Matters in a Diamond Bar Claim

items.title: California's Filing Deadline is Firm
items.desc: Most car accident injury claims in California must be filed within two years, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity, like a road maintained by Caltrans along SR-60 or SR-57, is involved.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning any percentage of blame assigned to you can reduce your compensation, so how the crash is documented from the start matters.

items.title: What You Say to an Insurer Can Follow You
items.desc: Giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company before speaking with an attorney can create problems later, since early evidence and witness accounts along busy stretches like Golden Springs Drive tend to fade quickly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Diamond Bar?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government-maintained road or vehicle was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth getting guidance early.

items.question: Does it matter that my crash happened near SR-60 or SR-57?
items.answer: Freeway interchange areas and connecting surface streets like Diamond Bar Boulevard often involve different agencies and insurance layers, which can affect how a claim is investigated. An independent attorney can help sort out which records and reports apply to your specific location.

items.question: Should I talk to the other driver's insurance company first?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney, since anything you say could be used to argue you were partly at fault under California's comparative fault rule. LawProactive can connect you with someone who can advise you on next steps before you respond to any insurer.
